messages.subject: Multivariate DLM -- how to improve mixing
parts:
Dear stanners,

I've been a happy user since version Stan 1.0. I am trying to implement a DLM of sorts with rstan 2.0.0 (in R 3.0.1), but I can't work out why the mixing is so slow and effective sample sizes so low on this occasion. I've tried every trick, including re-parametrizing along the lines of what is given in Chapter 19 of the manual. Please find stan code and sample data attached.

Thank you for your help.

Guy

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Multivariate DLM -- how to improve mixing
parts:
I just sent another post today that I think answers the
same questions (mainly with a promissory note that we're
still working on making multivariate models faster).

About all you can do at this point is
more vectorization --- that'll cut down on the number of
linear algebra solver operations that happen.

You can also play around with lowering the step size by
upping the acceptance probability target --- Michael's been
suggesting that for other models to help mixing.

And for your case here:

for (i in 1:I1180) { # for each test
# U1180stdmultinormal[i] ~ normal(0, 1);
X1180[i] ~ multi_normal(mu1180 + sigma1180decom * U1180stdmultinormal[i], me1180);
}

you can move the linear operation mu1180 + sigma1180decom * .... into
a single operation. That is, create the big mean vector from U1180stdmultinormal
and then add and multiply from there. This cuts down on the size of the
expression tree used for gradients and should speed things up a bit. But this
will be minor compared to the basic vectorization itself.

- Bob
